exposure: Elevated airway liquid volumes at birth (mimicking cesarean section)
Control airway liquid volumes at birth (mimicking vaginal delivery)
outcome: Lung function (ventilator parameters, compliance, lung gas volumes, and distribution of gas within the lung)
Inflation pressures to aerate the lung
Uniformity and distribution of lung aeration
cohort: Near-term newborn rabbit kittens (30 days gestation, term=32 days) with either control or elevated airway liquid volumes.
finding: Commencing ventilation with 8 cmH2O PEEP mitigated the adverse effects of elevated airway liquid volumes, increasing lung compliance, functional residual capacity, and the uniformity and distribution of lung aeration, although it did not normalize aeration of the distal airways.
mod_finding: The study investigated elevated airway liquid volumes that corresponded to cesarean section and control volumes corresponding to vaginal delivery, suggesting PEEP supports lung function in newborns at greater risk of respiratory distress due to elevated airway liquid volumes associated with C-section.
